**Synopsis:**
A global bond rout is deepening, driven by Middle East-conflict-fueled energy price spikes (Brent ~$95.61/bbl), persistent above-target inflation, massive AI-driven corporate bond issuance, and mounting sovereign debt concerns. US 10Y yields are at a near 3-year high of 4.81%, with 5% seen as the next critical threshold. Japan's 10Y hit a 30-year high above 3%, UK gilts at 2008 highs, and European bond futures at multi-decade lows. Markets are pricing a US rate hike (~68% probability) shortly, with Fed Chair Warsh sounding hawkish. Bond vigilante dynamics are intensifying, and financial repression (YCC/QE) is being floated as a tail-risk policy response.
